discovery: Optical metamaterials and metasurfaces: designing electromagnetic response through engineered subwavelength structure
motivation: Pendry showed theoretically that subwavelength structures can produce electromagnetic properties not found in natural materials: artificial magnetism, negative refraction, the perfect lens and transformation optics. Smith first demonstrated a negative-index metamaterial experimentally and, with Pendry, realised the electromagnetic cloak, turning these ideas into a new design principle for physics. Capasso brought the concept to flat optics. His generalised laws of refraction and reflection for phase-gradient metasurfaces made ultrathin metalenses and wavefront-shaping devices possible, and these are now being manufactured. Together their work changed how physicists control light. Material response became something to design, with applications ranging from fundamental near-field optics and analog optical computing to imaging, sensing, telecommunications and photovoltaics. Thousands of laboratories and industry now build on it. This is a rare case of deep conceptual originality reaching all the way into technology.
